items.title: Jackie Williams interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995
items.q: I wasn’t there in the beginning like say Milton or a lot of the other musicians were

ctx.x: Has recording, the process of it, changed significantly over the years, since you started recording? The actual studio presence?

Well I imagine it has come to a lot of technical changes. They use a lot more technologies now. I wasn’t there in the beginning like say Milton or a lot of the other musicians were, but I could tell that they utilize a lot more things, you know, machinery and microphoning and things like that — unless you tell them that you don’t want all that. You know sometimes you can tell them, if you’re being over miced or if there’s something wrong with the way they’re doing it, you could make suggestions. But they’re going…
Yeah. They say, “Yeah, yeah,” and then after you leave it’s like— © Fillius Jazz Archive -4-
